model: manual (Claude Code session acting as reviewer)

findings.title: First-time empty state shows no example of what the tool does
findings.description: A new visitor lands on an empty 'Your batches' panel with only a 'New batch' button. They must commit to filling the whole planner before seeing any value or understanding the timeline/vessel payoff. Leading with a visible example reduces first-action friction and is the strongest lever on engaged_sessions for a first-time-heavy audience.
findings.evidence: home_empty.png: the panel reads 'No batches yet. Click New batch to design your first one.' with no demo, thumbnail, or preview of an in-progress batch.
findings.suggested_change: Add a 'Try a sample batch' action on the empty state that loads a pre-filled demo batch (clearly labeled as a sample, dismissible) so visitors immediately see the vessel + timeline + stats before building their own.

findings.title: Technical terms have no inline explanation for beginners
findings.description: Stats read 'Starting gravity 1.140 / Est. final gravity 1.028 / Est. ABV 14.7%' with no explanation. v2's secondary audience is beginners; the strategy doc calls for tooltips on technical terms. Without them, beginners can't interpret the core output.
findings.evidence: planner_form.png and batch_detail.png: 'Starting gravity', 'Est. final gravity' shown as bare numbers with no affordance to learn what they mean.
findings.suggested_change: Add small info tooltips (keyboard-accessible) on gravity/ABV/phase terms with one-line plain-language explanations.

findings.title: Detail view doesn't tell the maker what to do today
findings.description: The batch detail shows a timeline and an observations log, but nothing tells the maker the next concrete action ('today: log a gravity reading', 'day 2: nutrient addition'). The decision-layer mission is 'what do I do today?'. Right now the page is passive.
findings.evidence: batch_detail.png: timeline + empty observations with the prompt 'No observations yet…' but no next-step guidance tied to where the batch is in its timeline.
findings.suggested_change: Add a small 'next step' line on the detail page derived from the current phase (e.g. lag → 'expect activity within 24-48h; log your first gravity reading').
